title: Prime-to-ell transfer proves degree-two vanishing for finite coefficients
statement: Using [def-exc-continuous-cohomology], let $G$ be a profinite group, $\ell$ a prime, and $M$ a finite discrete continuous $\ell$-primary $G$-module. Let $H\subseteq G$ be an open subgroup such that $H^2(H,M)=0$ and such that the finite index $[G:H]$ is prime to $\ell$. Then $H^2(G,M)=0$. More precisely, restriction from $G$ to $H$ followed by corestriction back to $G$ is multiplication by $[G:H]$ on $H^2(G,M)$; hence it is injective on this $\ell$-primary group, while its restriction is zero because $H^2(H,M)=0$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-group-h2-transfer-transfer-identity] with q=2. The restriction from H^2(G,M) to H^2(H,M), followed by corestriction, is multiplication by [G:H].

The restriction map is zero because H^2(H,M)=0, so the composite in Step 1 is zero. Since M is finite and ell-primary, some ell^r annihilates M; the cochain complex computing H^2(G,M) is therefore ell^r-torsion termwise, so ell^r annihilates H^2(G,M). Bézout gives integers a,b with a[G:H]+b ell^r=1 because [G:H] is prime to ell. For x in H^2(G,M), Step 1 gives [G:H]x=0, and hence x=(a[G:H]+b ell^r)x=0. Thus H^2(G,M)=0.
